question.problem: A bank manager notices that, on average, for each group of  customers, $9$ of them visit the cash machine. What is the probability that in the next group of customers, less than $5$ customers visit the cash machine? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that visits of cash machine occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of customers that visit the cash machine. Since the average rate is $9$ customers per group, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of customers that visit the cash machine can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =9,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(9).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{9}^{x}{e}^{-9}}{x!}
$$

Therefore, the probability that less than $5$ customers visit the cash machine in the next group is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 4) & =P(X\in {0,1,2,3,4}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =\frac{{9}^{0}{e}^{-9}}{0!}+\frac{{9}^{1}{e}^{-9}}{1!}+\frac{{9}^{2}{e}^{-9}}{2!}+\frac{{9}^{3}{e}^{-9}}{3!}+\frac{{9}^{4}{e}^{-9}}{4!} \\  & ≈0.055\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
